gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Tektur has a pipe-cleaner look, with every curve left open at its ends and a lowercase that runs oversized. Noto Sans Grantha takes the opposite job, with tall little letters and bowls that never close up and snag the eye.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Tektur draws everything with a constant stroke from top to baseline, its curves left generously open at the ends. Big and short is where it earns its keep.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Cut like laser-etched sheet metal. Tektur keeps one cutting width throughout, while Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of the line height with open-ended lowercase that is easy to follow.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Expressive is the first word for Tektur, whose round bowls keep their walls uniform and whose lowercase is oversized. Noto Sans Hebrew does the quieter work, with a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-hk: Distinctive from the first letter, Tektur looks drawn with one nib and leaves its curve endings wide open. Noto Sans HK follows with large lowercase forms and brush ends that lift away before each curve closes.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aram: Tektur brings pipe-cleaner strokes that stay one width, with openings at the end of every curve and an oversized lowercase. And Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic is approachable in return, its c ending in open pincers and its capitals only a short step above the lowercase.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian reads with big open eyes on every e and a, and a deep band between baseline and mean line. Tektur, by contrast, stays showy.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-jp: Tektur cuts its letters like an engraver, one depth throughout, with open curve ends and outsized lowercase. Noto Sans JP, with its very tall x-height, probably wants a modest size.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Tektur looks drawn with a rounded nib, with no swelling at stroke ends and generous openings on every curve. Noto Sans Kaithi meets it with an open-channeled e and lowercase that fills the line like capitals.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Tektur outlines every letter with one steady thickness, leaving its curves open and its lowercase oversized. Noto Sans Kannada, with its gentle bump up to capitals, would sit happily at a modest size.
